parsed.summary: The netlist implements exactly the architecture the specification describes (24V→5V buck U7/TPS62933 → 5V→3.3V LDO U9/AZ1117; two ADM3260 isolators U2/U6 bridging the main I2C to the isolated pH/EC EZO circuits while the RTD EZO M2 shares the non-isolated bus; three TMC2209 drivers U8/U10/U11 on a shared single-wire UART with per-driver 5VOUT current-reference dividers and 110 mΩ sense resistors; IRLR2905 main-pump and N-MOSFET ATO-valve low-side switches with BT3904 interlocks; SMBJ28A TVS and 7 A fuse on the 24 V input). All apparent differences from the spec's component table (M1↔M4, U3/U4↔U2/U6, U5–U7↔U8/U10/U11, L1↔L2, F1↔F2, D2↔D1, etc.) are the reference-number permutations the spec itself documents, and the unwired TF-Luna, DNP BME280/BH1750, missing DS18B20 net, and firmware-GPIO mismatch are explicitly listed as known limitations, not faults. Passive values, ratings, pull directions (e.g. valve gate pull-down R49 to GND) and the ADM3260 VSEL divider (R46/R4 and R30/R48, which biases VSEL above the high threshold to select the isolated +5 V the EZO circuits need) are all consistent with the intended design, so no anomaly is supported by the files.

Let's carefully examine the netlist. The spec describes components with references: M1 ESP32-C6-DevKitC-1-N8, M2 EZO-pH, M3 EZO-EC, M4 EZO-RTD, U3/U4 ADM3260, U5/U6/U7 TMC2209, U1 TPS62933, U2 AZ1117-3.3, T2 IRLR2905, T3 AON6407, D2 SMBJ28A TVS, F1 7A fuse, D1/D4 SS34.

Hold on, maybe I mis-assigned. Let's look at H11 and H13 (2-pos MC connectors). H11 pin1 on +24V, pin2 on NET0084 (T6 drain). H13 pin1 on +24V, pin2 on NET0016 (T2 drain). T2 = AO3400A N-MOSFET. In netlist, IRLR2905 is T6, gate via R6 100 ohm, pre-driven via T5 BT3904. So functionally IRLR2905 main pump exists but with different refs. OK.

Spec says "T3 — AON6407 (8-DFN N-MOSFET) ... drives ATO_VALVE net; gate driven through R10 (100 Ω), pre-driven via T4 (BT3904)." In netlist, AON6407 is T4 but it's a P-channel high-side switch on the 24V rail, not a low-side ATO valve switch. And there's an AO3400A T2 low-side switch driving H13 with gate via R21 100 ohm pre-driven via T1 BT3904 — that matches the *structure* of the ATO valve low-side switch (gate 100 ohm, BT3904 pre-drive), but uses AO3400A instead of AON6407, and the AON6407 is repurposed as a high-side rail switch.

Hmm, but is that an anomaly or just a redesign? The spec is "derived from examining the reference design". The spec describes intended design: ATO valve low-side switch with AON6407 N-MOSFET. The netlist shows AON6407 as P-channel high-side switch controlling the entire 24V rail, and the ATO-valve-position low-side switch is an AO3400A. That would make the board behave differently: the 24V rail to all loads (pumps, valve, TMC2209 VS, buck input) is now switched by a P-FET from an ESP32 GPIO, instead of being always-on with only the valve switched. That's a huge behavioral difference: firmware toggling the ATO valve GPIO would instead cut power to the whole 24V rail (including main pump and dosing drivers). That seems like a serious anomaly.

But wait, let's double check the gate drive of T4. NET0017: D2 zener cathode, R9 pin1, T4 pin1 G. R9 pin2 on /+24V_{F}. So R9 33k from source to gate (pull-up for P-FET, keeps it off). D2 zener 12V between gate and GND? D2 pin1 K on gate, pin2 A on GND. So zener clamps gate to ~12V above GND? For a P-FET with source at 24V, to turn on you need gate below source by Vgs(th), e.g., gate at 12V gives Vgs = -12V, on. To turn off, gate must be near source (24V). But the gate is pulled to 24V via R9 (source is 24V side). So off when nothing drives gate. To turn on, something must pull gate down to ~12V. What connects to NET0017 besides R9 and D2? Only those three nodes: D2 pin1, R9 pin1, T4 pin1. There's NO gate drive from a transistor or ESP32! The gate is only connected to R9 (to source) and D2 (zener to GND). So T4 can never be turned on by the MCU; it's floating except pull-up. Actually D2 zener to GND would clamp gate to 12V only if gate is pulled above 12V; but gate is pulled to 24V via R9, so zener conducts and holds gate at ~12V (zener breakdown from cathode to anode? cathode at gate, anode at GND; if gate >12V, zener breaks down clamping gate to 12V). So gate sits at 12V, source at 24V => Vgs = -12V => P-FET is permanently ON. So T4 is effectively a permanent short (always on) between fuse and 24V rail, with no control. That means the 24V rail is always on (good, matches spec that 24V rail powers everything), but the AON6407 is being used as a reverse-polarity or soft-start switch? Actually with gate clamped at 12V it's always on. Hmm but then there's no MCU control on it. That might be intentional as a high-side switch for e.g. inrush limiting or reverse polarity protection? Not described.

But the bigger issue: the AON6407 high-side switch T4 has its gate not driven by MCU (only R9+D2). If it's always on, then it's just a pass element; not a behavioral anomaly per se, but the spec intended AON6407 to be the valve switch. The valve is now on AO3400A. Now is the high-side AON6407 an anomaly? It's an extra component not in spec's architecture (spec has no high-side switch on 24V rail; F1 fuse directly to +24V). The netlist inserts T4 between fuse and the 24V rail. If T4 is always on (gate clamped 12V), then it's just a conductor; but if it were meant to be controlled, it's mis-wired. But more importantly, the AON6407 P-FET used as high-side with source on /+24V_F (fuse side) and drain on +24V: the body diode of a P-FET points from drain to source? For P-channel, source is the higher potential normally; here source=24V (after fuse), drain=24V rail. When on, current flows source->drain (from fuse to rail) which is the normal direction? P-FET conducts from source to drain when on; source must be higher potential. Here source (24V_F) and drain (24V rail) same potential; the FET just passes current from fuse to rail. Body diode orientation: P-FET body diode anode at drain, cathode at source (since it's a P-channel, the diode points from drain to source? Actually for a P-FET, the body diode conducts from source to drain? Let's recall: N-FET body diode anode=source, cathode=drain (conducts source->drain? no, conducts drain->source? Hmm). For N-channel MOSFET, body diode anode is source, cathode is drain, so it conducts when drain > source (reverse of normal current). Wait normal N-FET current flows drain->source; body diode conducts source->drain (i.e., when source higher). For P-FET, body diode anode drain, cathode source, conducts drain->source (when drain higher than source). In our case source=24V_F (input side), drain=+24V rail (output side). If input present, source=24V, output caps charge to 24V, no difference. If input removed but output has charge (caps), drain > source, body diode conducts drain->source, back-feeding into fuse side. Not great but minor.
